Subject: Multi-stage upgrade & fallback ladder — Private (VPC)

Team,

Summary: proposing a staged, low-risk upgrade process for Skyline Health's Private deployment (VPC) that emphasizes version pinning, short maintenance windows, and an explicit fallback "ladder" so we can recover quickly without data loss. High-level asks: alignment on maintenance window, sign-off on the fallback ladder, and confirmation of audit/export requirements.

Proposal (high level)
- Phase 0 (preflight, 48–72h before): export audit logs, run preflight smoke checklist, snapshot VM images where applicable.
- Phase 1 (canary): patch 1–2 canary nodes in us-west2 (non-primary availability zone), 1–2 hour window; run full smoke and latency/regression checks.
- Phase 2 (gradual roll): 25% -> 50% -> 100% with traffic shifting over 2–4 hours per step depending on metrics.
- Version pinning: pin control plane to major.minor (e.g., 1.8) and allowed patch range (1.8.x). Production pin will be set to 1.8.3 and we will only promote 1.8.4 after successful canaries.
- Fallback ladder (ordered):
  1) Immediate traffic cut to previous image (fast switch via routing rules).
  2) If routing switch insufficient, roll nodes back to pinned image (automated snapshot restore).
  3) If state corruption suspected, cut to Redwood-hosted fallback (temporary hosted model) while we onboard a hotfix.

Networking / security notes
- Ensure NAT gateway egress rules allow scaling hosts to reach Redwood control plane during rollout.
- Firewall stanzas: maintain static egress to management endpoints; we'll provide final CIDR list.
- KV cache invalidation: in-canary we will explicitly clear prefix cache for test namespaces only.

Attachments and artifacts
- attached: staged-upgrade-ladder-v1.xlsx (matrix of steps, rollback triggers, owners)
- preflight-smoke-checklist.md (link/checklist) -> https://drive.google.com/open?id=1A2bUpgradeLadderDoc
- JIRA: INF-8421 created for runbook automation tasks

Questions for recipients
- Ops (Skyline): preferred maintenance windows and notification/notice SLA?
- Lauren: any customer comms cadence constraints?
- Karthik/Olga: confirm firewall/CIDR change windows and whether we can automate snapshot restores within SLA.

I propose a tentative canary on Thu Sep 30 02:00–05:00 ET (overnight) with full roll target Mon Oct 4 if canaries are green. If Skyline needs a different window, call it out.

Thanks,
Rishi

Rishi / team — technical caveats from infra: 
- Canary targets: pick nodes that are behind non-critical LB pools and with isolated NVMe (we don't want shared drives during canary restores). Recommend 2 nodes in us-west2 and 1 node in us-east1 as cross-region sanity.
- Rolling snapshots: snapshot restore time for the current storage profile averages 9–12 minutes/node; include that into rollback SLA planning.
- Network: we'll need to pre-authorize the Redwood control-plane CIDRs; I'll send the final list by EOD. Avoid touching customer side DBs during the roll — all schema migrations must be out-of-band.
- Health checks: smoke should verify: model load success, KV cache hits <5% delta, tail-latency <150ms p50/p95 targets.

Two asks:
1) Ops: confirm blackout windows for config pushes (some firewalls only accept pushes during low-traffic windows)
2) Rishi: add a step to capture in-flight request handoff behavior (how we drain connection pools during routing cut)
